q: Batteries and generators are called sources of _____ force.
e: Batteries and generators are sources of electromotive force.

q: A battery converts _____ energy into electrical energy to provide electrical power.
e: A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy.

q: In an electric generator, _____ energy is converted into electrical energy.
e: In an electric generator, mechanical energy is converted into electrical energy.

q: The main function of the source is to send negative charges from the positive terminal to the _____ terminal within the source.
e: The main function is to send negative charges from the positive to the negative terminal.

q: Electromotive force is the amount of energy provided by the battery per unit charge to move round the _____ circuit.
e: Electromotive force is the energy per unit charge to move round the complete circuit.

q: The unit of electromotive force is volt, equivalent to _____ per coulomb of electric charge.
e: Volt is equivalent to joule per coulomb ($J C^{-1}$).

q: Despite its name, electromotive force is not actually a _____.
e: Despite its name, electromotive force is not actually a force.

q: The internal resistance of a battery depends on its size, chemical properties, life time, and _____.
e: Internal resistance depends on size, chemical properties, life time, and temperature.

q: A battery which has an internal resistance $r$ must be viewed as having a resistor of resistance $r$ connected in _____ to the battery.
e: The internal resistance is regarded as being connected in series to the battery.

q: The equation $E = IR + Ir$ is called the _____ equation.
e: The equation $E = IR + Ir$ is called the circuit equation.

q: The potential difference across the terminals of a battery connected to an external circuit is called the _____ voltage.
e: It is called the terminal voltage or available voltage.

q: Electromotive force (emf) is the potential difference between the two terminals of a battery in an _____ circuit.
e: Emf is the potential difference in an open circuit when no current flows.

q: Terminal voltage is the potential difference between the two terminals of a battery in a _____ circuit.
e: Terminal voltage is the potential difference in a closed circuit.

q: When a battery having an internal resistance is used in an electric circuit, the potential difference between the terminals is always _____ than its emf.
e: The terminal potential difference is always less than its emf when discharging.

q: When charging a battery, the potential difference between the terminals is equal to _____.
e: When charging, the potential difference is $V = E + Ir$.

q: The potential difference or voltage is the amount of energy required to move a unit charge from one end to another end of a circuit _____.
e: Voltage is the energy required to move a unit charge across a circuit element.

q: In charging a battery, the chemical energy which has been used up is supplied back by _____ energy from some external source.
e: Chemical energy used up is supplied back by electrical energy during charging.

q: A steady current will flow through the conductor if a steady _____ difference is maintained between its ends.
e: A steady current flows if a steady potential difference is maintained.

q: The positive charges are sent from the negative terminal to the _____ terminal within the source.
e: Positive charges are sent from the negative to the positive terminal within the source.

q: By Ohm's law, the potential difference across the resistor is $V =$ _____.
e: By Ohm's law, the potential difference across the resistor is $V = IR$.

q: The total work done in moving a unit positive charge round the complete circuit is _____, which is the emf $E$ of the battery.
e: The total work done is $IR + Ir$, which equals the emf $E$.

q: The internal resistance of a battery is represented by the symbol _____.
e: Internal resistance is represented by the lowercase symbol $r$.

q: The emf of a battery is represented by the symbol _____.
e: Electromotive force is represented by the symbol $E$.

q: The work done in moving a unit positive charge from one end to another of the internal resistance $r$ of the battery is _____.
e: The work done across the internal resistance is $Ir$.

q: In an open circuit, the terminal voltage $V$ is related to emf $E$ by the equation $V =$ _____.
e: In an open circuit, no current flows, so $V = E$.

q: When a battery is charging, the terminal voltage $V$ is _____ than its emf $E$.
e: When charging, $V = E + Ir$, so $V$ is greater than $E$.
